title: Regenerate gamut's audit artifact — three files still publish the 89% figure
description:
PUBLISHED ERROR, still live after #13. That PR fixed the measurement — gamut now measures the funnel at the depth it says it measured, and the depth-100 window is gone from the code — but it could not regenerate the artifact, and said so: its own review raised this at severity high and dispositioned it 'ignored' because regeneration needs cadence/data, a 15GB download absent from every worktree.

So gamut/artifacts/audit_report.json still records depth 100 with no funnel block, and three files still publish the number derived from it:

  gamut/artifacts/results.html   '89% of the catalog that ...'
  gamut/README.md                '89% of the catalog that never became a candidate'
  docs/INTENT.md                 '89% of the catalog never becomes a candidate'

The real figure is ~29%. Union reach is 70.6% at 1500 (what retrieve returns) against the 10.7% at depth 100 that was measured and labelled 'Reached by retrieval'. Independently re-verified at n=60: 26.9/11.4/2.7, the same order-of-magnitude error.

This is not a builder's to close. It needs the dataset, so it needs a machine that has it.
design:
1. Fetch cadence/data (~15GB).
2. gamut collect at the real depth, then gamut audit — #13 added a matching --depth to audit so the pair no longer raises an unrecoverable ValueError.
3. Commit the regenerated audit_report.json.
4. Re-read every published number from it: results.html, gamut/README.md, docs/INTENT.md. Do not hand-edit 89% to 29% — the point of the funnel block is that the page reads the artifact.
acceptance_criteria: audit_report.json records the real depth and carries a funnel block. No file in the repo states 89% except as a recorded correction. A check-claims run passes against the regenerated artifact — that target exists to catch exactly this drift between a page and the numbers behind it.
close_reason: Regenerated on the data host at depth 1500 and all literals moved in one commit (e1d535c). pool reach 10.7%->70.6%, never-a-candidate 89%->29%, Gini floor 0.936->0.932. Headline softened from 'you cannot re-rank your way out of a retrieval problem' to 're-ranking moves exposure far less than the pool composition does' -- direction survives, strength does not. Published page republished. Note: spot-ge2 counted docs/INTENT.md as a third publication site, but it quotes the figure to retract it.

title: Regenerate Gamut at true depth and flip its published literals in one commit
description:
Second half of spot-ph0, split out because it cannot be done in a builder worktree. spot-ph0 fixed the mechanism (gamut depth now derives from cadence fused_candidates=1500, the cache refuses a shallower window, the report publishes a stage-labelled funnel). It could not regenerate the artifact: gamut/artifacts/audit_report.json still says config.depth 100 and pool.track_coverage 10.7%, so results.html still ships the bar labelled 'Reached by retrieval: 10.7%' and the published error is still live.

WHY THIS IS ONE COMMIT AND NOT THREE. check_claims verifies the root README against the artifact. It passes today only because BOTH are wrong in the same way. Regenerate without editing the README and lint-all goes red; edit the README without regenerating and it goes red the other way. Artifact and literals have to move together.

NEEDS THE DATA HOST: cadence/data/processed (a ~15 GB download plus the build pipeline). No worktree has it.

STEPS:
1. make -C gamut collect audit report   (collect is now 1500 deep, ~15x the old work)
2. Expect config.depth 1500, baseline.pool.track_coverage ~0.706, and a funnel block with retrieved/read_by_select/shown at 1500/500/20.
3. results.html and gamut/docs/RESULTS.md regenerate themselves, including the '89% never becomes a candidate' sentence, which is computed from pool.track_coverage and becomes ~29%.
4. Hand-edit, in the SAME commit: root README.md '10.7%'; scripts/check_claims.py Claim('gamut', '10.7%', ...); gamut/README.md's '10.71%' row and its '89% of the catalog' sentence.
5. The 0.936 floor ALSO moves. rerank and apply_artist_cap now see 1500-wide blocks, so the frontier and caps are recomputed over 15x the candidates; docs/INTENT.md records 0.9321 at true depth, past the floor the page calls the limit of all thirteen interventions, at 62% of R-precision instead of 15%. Update the check_claims '0.936' claim, the root README block quote and gamut/README.md's 'moves only from 0.951 to 0.936' together. The direction of the finding survives; the number does not.
6. gamut/scripts/build_report.py:418 hardcodes 're-ordering a hundred candidates' - it is now fifteen hundred.
7. Consider registering gamut/README.md's own numbers with check_claims: it only reads the root README, which is why that page could publish the top-100 window indefinitely with nothing to catch it.

ACCEPTANCE: config.depth 1500 and baseline.pool.track_coverage > 0.70 in the artifact; a funnel block with three stages carrying their depths; every literal above updated; make lint-all green in the same commit.
acceptance_criteria: audit_report.json has config.depth 1500 and baseline.pool.track_coverage > 0.70; a funnel block with three depth-carrying stages; the 10.7% and 0.936 literals updated in root README, check_claims.py and gamut/README.md; make lint-all green in the same commit

Headline softened from 'you cannot re-rank your way out of a retrieval problem' to 're-ranking moves exposure far less than the pool composition does' -- direction survives, strength does not. Published page republished. Note: spot-ge2 counted docs/INTENT.md as a third publication site, but it quotes the figure to retract it.

title: Two closed beads' work is off main, and the fleet closer that did it is out of reach
description:
Found by scripts/reconcile_board.py --audit while building spot-e11, on 2026-09-04.

The fleet's reconcile-board (fw-y1y, which lives outside this repo) closed two beads today on merges that never reached main:

  spot-7lj  closed 20:37:51Z  PR #9   merged into fleet/builder-permissions  (merge 1aa2702)
  spot-4gd  closed 20:37:49Z  PR #10  merged into bead/spot-2ig              (merge c3772dd)

Neither merge commit is an ancestor of refs/remotes/origin/main; both were verified with git merge-base --is-ancestor. This is spot-e11's defect recurring, and spot-ln4's stranding recurring, twice, after both were filed.

spot-4gd matters beyond itself: spot-yld declares a dependency on spot-4gd, so with spot-4gd closed the board reports spot-yld as ready while the tag matrix work it builds on is not on main. PR #10's base is bead/spot-2ig, a bead branch -- the ADR 0009 child-PR trap, one level deeper than PR #4's.

spot-e11 gives this repo a correct reconcile-board and the --audit that found this, but it cannot fix fw-y1y (different repository) and does not reopen closed beads or merge anything -- both are the human's call under ADR 0003.

NEEDS A HUMAN DECISION: (a) how each merge reaches main -- cherry-pick onto main in a new PR, since a rebase would replay work already upstream; (b) whether to reopen spot-7lj and spot-4gd until it does; (c) the fw-y1y fix, which has to happen in the flywheel repo or every builder here keeps getting mis-closed.
acceptance_criteria: Both merge commits are ancestors of origin/main, or their beads are reopen with a note saying why; 'make reconcile-board ARGS=--audit' exits 0; and fw-y1y either checks the merge target or is retired in favour of this repo's reconcile-board.
notes:
Do not close this by reopening the beads alone -- the audit must go green, which means the commits actually reach main.
Builder fleet/builder-py checked spot-3wy: no build work remains for a builder here. PR #14 (fix/recover-stranded-tests, opened by James Ponwith) already contains the cherry-picked recovery of PR #9 (spot-7lj) and PR #10 (spot-4gd)'s content, satisfies decision (a) from this bead's description, and is green: gh pr checks 14 shows lint + all five app test suites passing, and the PR body reports cadence rc=0, gamut rc=0, make lint-all rc=0. PR #14 is OPEN, unmerged -- merging is the human's call under ADR 0003, so I did not claim or build against this bead. Once #14 merges, both merge commits become ancestors of origin/main and 'make reconcile-board ARGS=--audit' should be re-run to confirm it exits 0. Still outstanding and explicitly human-decision per the bead text: (b) whether/how to reopen spot-7lj and spot-4gd before #14 merges, and (c) the fw-y1y fix in the flywheel repo, which is out of this repo's scope. Leaving bead open.
Builder fleet/builder-py ended as no-op having committed nothing; the spawner returned this bead to open so it is allocatable again (fw-lb8.7). See .flywheel/runs/spotify-recsys-ecosystem-spot-3wy.log.
close_reason: Both strandings recovered by PR #14 (a2ca2b9), verified on main rather than taken on report: cadence/eval/run_eval.py carries the paired-delta support from spot-7lj, models/train.py:180 writes tags_train.npz and catalog.py:61 prefers it from spot-4gd, and their tests (test_paired_eval.py, test_catalog_load.py) pass on main. The dependent bead spot-yld is therefore genuinely ready rather than falsely ready. The recurrence-prevention half is spot-e11's, closed separately -- it belongs to the Go reconcile-board in the flywheel repo, not here.

title: Close-on-merge must check the merge TARGET, not just that a merge happened
description:
spot-2ig was closed on 2026-08-30 with reason 'PR #4 merged', and its work was not on main for a day.

PR #4's base was fleet/builder-permissions, not main. That integration branch had already reached main via the EARLIER PR #3, so nothing merged it forward again. Five commits sat on it -- lexicon_calibration.json, eval/lexicon_audit.py, its tests, and 92 lines of FINDINGS -- while the board reported the bead shipped. A clone of main did not contain any of it.

Nothing was lost and the merge was clean (pushed as 2473b49, 0 stranded commits remaining). The defect is in the accounting: 'a PR merged' was treated as 'the work shipped', and those are only the same thing when the PR's base is the released branch.

Compounding it, the fleet's own merge targets are inconsistent: PR #4 based on fleet/builder-permissions, PR #6 (spot-ktp) based on main.

This is the repo's recurring pattern again -- a signal whose stated meaning is stronger than its actual meaning. Closed meant merged; merged did not mean shipped.

ESTABLISHES: that a closed bead's work is reachable from main. DOES NOT: prevent a bead being closed for other reasons, or address whether fleet branches should target main directly.
acceptance_criteria: reconcile-board resolves the PR's baseRefName and only closes when the merge commit is an ancestor of origin/main; a bead whose PR merged to a non-released branch stays open with a note naming the branch. Regression: replay spot-2ig's situation (PR merged to a non-main base) and assert the bead is NOT closed.
notes: PR #12 closed unmerged: it reimplemented reconcile-board in Python, and this repo is already covered by the flywheel's Go tool. The diagnosis and the stronger reachability test were correct and are being carried into that tool as fw-n1r; nothing here needs a second implementation. Reopened so it can be closed against whatever lands, or closed as superseded once fw-n1r ships.
close_reason:
Resolved elsewhere, deliberately not here. The defect was real and recurred three times after filing (spot-2ig, then spot-7lj and spot-4gd). The fix was built as scripts/reconcile_board.py on bead/spot-e11 and PR #12 was CLOSED WITHOUT MERGING by the maintainer, with reason: reconcile-board already exists as a Go tool in the flywheel repo which has this repository in its roster, so merging would leave two implementations of one policy in two languages -- the same 'two homes for one thing' argument ADR 0017 used against OpenSpec.

The idea was taken rather than dropped. The Python version asked 'is the merge commit reachable from origin/main now?' where the Go tool asked 'did it merge into the default branch?' -- strictly stronger, and the difference is real here because main was force-pushed on 2026-08-27, rewriting 25 commits, so anything merged before that has a correct baseRefName and is no longer reachable. Filed as fw-n1r against the Go tool, citing PR #12 as the source.

Closing here because no work remains that this repository can do. bead/spot-e11 is left unmerged on purpose; do not merge it forward.

title: Make the coverage tools fail instead of silently checking nothing
description:
Sixth and seventh instances of the repo's recurring pattern - a tool whose stated scope and actual scope differ.

VERIFIED: check_claims.py excludes missing_src from its exit condition, so moving artifacts aside prints '13/18 claims match' and EXITS 0. Since every app's `make clean` deletes artifacts/*.json, `make clean && make lint-all` is green while verifying nothing. Separately, Makefile:15 guards each app with `if [ -x $a/.venv/bin/ruff ]`, so an app with no venv is skipped silently and exits 0.

Also verified: cadence/Makefile lints `src tests` where the other four apps lint `src tests scripts`, and cadence/scripts has TWO unformatted files right now while `make -C cadence lint` exits 0.

ESTABLISHES: that green means checked. DOES NOT: find new drift - it makes existing checks honest about their own scope.

ACCEPTANCE: check_claims.py exits non-zero when any registered artifact is missing; lint-all exits non-zero when any app in APPS lacks a venv; cadence's lint target covers src tests scripts and its two unformatted files are fixed; both reproducers re-run clean.

Effort: 50 min.

title: Audit MOOD_LEXICON's audio targets against where humans actually file each word
description:
The mood-vs-genre argument may not be about the weight at all. VERIFIED: of 106 (word, dimension) pairs where the word is also a real tag, 72 assert a target FURTHER from the folksonomy's own mean than the plain catalog mean is - worse than doing nothing.

  sleep    energy           asserted 0.12  humans 0.509  catalog 0.632
  study    instrumentalness asserted 0.62  humans 0.279  catalog 0.099
  acoustic acousticness     asserted 0.85  humans 0.481  catalog 0.270
  happy    valence          asserted 0.85  humans 0.536  catalog 0.472

This explains why the audio term underperforms noise at strength: it is aimed somewhere humans do not put this music.

ESTABLISHES: how far apart the two definitions of each mood word are. DOES NOT: establish the lexicon is wrong - someone asking for 'chill' may well want calmer music than the median playlist titled chill. The folksonomy mean describes behaviour, not intent. Says nothing about the weight itself.

ACCEPTANCE: artifacts/lexicon_calibration.json with target / folksonomy_mean / catalog_mean / n_tracks per pair, plus the count where |target-folksonomy| > |catalog-folksonomy|; top-20 table in docs/FINDINGS.md; runs under 60s.

Effort: 45 min. Reads only tags.npz, tag_vocab.json, tracks.parquet - no engine.
notes: Reopened: PR #4 merged into fleet/builder-permissions, not main. Its merge commit is not reachable from origin/main and the lexicon audit is on no branch that will merge again. reconcile-board closed it because gh reported MERGED without asking WHERE.
close_reason: PR #4 merged: spot-2ig: audit MOOD_LEXICON's audio targets against the folksonomy — closed by fleet reconcile-board; the fleet never merges, so this is how the merge reaches the board (fw-y1y)

title: Fix Gamut's per-channel sentinel - lexical's row IS the baseline row
description:
PUBLISHED ERROR. gamut/src/gamut/audit.py:38 treats ranks[i] >= 0 as 'this channel returned this candidate'. cadence/src/cadence/retrieval/fusion.py:78 fills absent candidates with depth+1, not -1, so the sentinel passes the filter and each channel block is the whole pool re-sorted.

VERIFIED contamination of stored channel ranks: tag 33.7%, cooccurrence 52.0%, lexical 57.1%, tag_exact 64.3%, collaborative 66.0%, popularity 71.5%, audio 88.3%.

This is why lexical's published row (R-prec 0.0227, gini 0.953, top1% 43.7%) is indistinguishable from baseline (0.0229, 0.951, 43.6%) - it IS the baseline row.

ESTABLISHES: which channel actually concentrates exposure. DOES NOT: disturb the two headline claims - tag_exact is uncontaminated, so 'the most accurate channel is the most concentrated' stands, as does the collaborative/cooccurrence dead-channel finding.

ACCEPTANCE: a test in gamut/tests asserting no channel block contains a candidate at the sentinel rank; the regenerated lexical row differs from baseline on R-precision and long-tail share.

Effort: 30 min.

title: Persist per-challenge metric vectors and report paired deltas
description:
run_eval.py gives every arm the identical challenge list in identical order and MetricAccumulator.values already holds the per-challenge vector; summary() collapses it to mean+SE and discards it. The pairing is generated on every run and thrown away.

Measured per-challenge correlation between arms is rho 0.9922-0.9995, so pairing buys 128-2171x variance reduction for ZERO extra compute. Detection floor at k=0 goes 0.0149 (10.4% of the metric) -> 0.00045-0.00185 (0.32-1.29%).

ESTABLISHES: that any two configs can be discriminated at effect sizes the current floor calls null. DOES NOT: change the SE of any absolute number (0.1429 +/- 0.0149 stays), prove any shipped value optimal, or touch assembly config, which this harness never executes.

ACCEPTANCE: re-running `cadence evaluate --limit 400` reproduces current means exactly and adds {metric}_delta / _delta_se / n_changed per arm; the sidecar re-derives every mean in eval_report.json to 1e-9; no_cooccurrence at k=5 reports paired 2SE strictly below the published unpaired 0.0204.

Effort: 45 min. Blocks most other measurement work.

title: Correct Gamut's funnel - it measured depth 100 and labelled it 'retrieval'
description:
PUBLISHED ERROR. gamut config depth=100; cadence fused_candidates=1500. Gamut measured the top 100 of a 1500-deep pool and labelled that bar 'Reached by retrieval'.

Union reach: 70.6% at 1500 (what retrieve returns), 38.4% at 500 (what select reads), 10.7% at 100 (what gamut measured), 3.0% shown. Independently verified at n=60: 26.9/11.4/2.7 - same order-of-magnitude error.

So the published '89% of the catalog never becomes a candidate' is arithmetic on the wrong denominator; the real figure is ~29%. A pilot at true depth pushes artist Gini to 0.9321, PAST the 0.936 floor the page calls the limit of all thirteen interventions - at 62% of R-precision instead of 15%.

ESTABLISHES: that the headline was measured on a window 15x shallower than the pool. DOES NOT: overturn the direction - concentration is still upstream of ranking - and does not make any point on the deeper frontier worth buying.

ACCEPTANCE: audit_report.json has config.depth 1500 and baseline.pool.track_coverage > 0.70; the funnel row and the 10.7% literal in root README and check_claims.py are corrected; check_claims passes.

Effort: 45 min.
notes:
builder: root cause is two hand-copies of one constant (gamut config depth=100, cli --depth 100) against cadence fused_candidates=1500. Fix derives depth from cadence.config.RetrievalConfig; cache load refuses a cache shallower than the depth being reported; report gains a stage-labelled funnel. Artifact regeneration needs cadence/data (absent in worktree, ~15GB download) - assessing.
PR #13 opened: depth derives from cadence fused_candidates, cache refuses a shallower window, report publishes a stage-labelled funnel. Gate green (26 tests, lint, 18 claims). title: Fix the reranker's training seeds - the 2026-08-21 fix was incomplete
description:
eval/splits.py was corrected on 2026-08-21 to take a playlist's genuine first k tracks instead of its k lowest track ids. models/reranker.py:205 still does the old thing:

    trs = interactions.indices[interactions.indptr[row] : interactions.indptr[row+1]]

So evaluation seeds were fixed and TRAINING seeds were not. The reranker roughly doubles k=0 R-precision (0.0709 -> 0.1429) - the single biggest win in the system - and is supervised on head-biased, unordered prefixes. artifacts/reranker.pkl (2026-08-15) predates order.npz (2026-08-21) by six days.

All five call sites were grepped: build.py and train.py use np.tile into the tag matrix and timbre's loader builds a filtered set - all three order-independent and correct. Exactly one real miss.

ESTABLISHES: whether Cadence's biggest win is trained on the same prefix definition it is evaluated on. DOES NOT: guarantee improvement - the reranker may get worse, and that must be published either way.

ACCEPTANCE: reranker.py obtains seeds via the same order.npz helper splits.py uses; reranker_meta.json regenerated; full_reranked reported before and after with paired deltas.

Effort: 60-90 min.
notes:
Released by hand. The 90-minute run ceiling killed 'fleet run' itself, so neither the builder's abandon path nor the coordinator's cleanup ran — the bead kept its in_progress status with no expiring lease, and reclaim correctly refuses those because that rule protects a human's work. Its branch carries 0 commits, so nothing was lost.

This is fw-lb8.7's case reached through the wall-clock rather than the turn cap: run.go recovers a bead when a BUILDER is killed, but not when the process supervising them is.

title: Move the CI workflow to the repo root, where GitHub will read it
description:
The repo's only workflow is cadence/.github/workflows/ci.yml and it is tracked. GitHub Actions reads .github/workflows only at the REPOSITORY ROOT, and the root has no .github directory - so the repo's only CI has never run a single job while presenting a complete lint/typecheck/test pipeline.

Double-blocked: `git check-ignore -v .github/workflows/ci.yml` returns `.gitignore:4:/*`, so the root whitelist would silently exclude a workflow added in the right place. Needs `!/.github/` alongside the existing !/Makefile and !/scripts/ entries.

Two further gaps to fix in the move: the lint step mirrors cadence's narrow `src tests` scope, and the coverage run passes --cov with no --cov-fail-under, so coverage is measured and then ignored.

ESTABLISHES: that CI runs at all. DOES NOT: improve any check - it makes the existing ones execute.

ACCEPTANCE: .github/workflows/ci.yml at the repo root, not matched by git check-ignore, running make lint-all plus each app's make test.

Effort: 45 min. Goes red immediately unless the coverage and lint items land first.
notes:
Partly overtaken: the root .github/ whitelist entry and a working root pr.yml landed in PR #3 (lint + a pytest matrix over all five apps, both green). What remains is the real find and it stands — cadence/.github/workflows/ci.yml is tracked, sits where GitHub Actions never looks, and presents a complete lint/typecheck/test pipeline that has never run a single job. Two jobs declared, zero executed, ever.

Also confirmed: it passes --cov with no --cov-fail-under, so even if it had run, coverage was measured and discarded — the same shape as spot-p7s, 'make the coverage tools fail instead of silently checking nothing'.

Narrowed scope: delete or fold the orphan into the root workflow, and decide what its coverage threshold should actually be.

title: Add cadence eval-ab and price rrf_k and the seven channel weights
description:
A command taking two config overrides, one seed count and a limit, running both arms over the same challenges with the same planned intents, reporting mean_a, mean_b, paired delta, paired SE and a detectable/not verdict.

At the existing n=400 this resolves 0.0013-0.0023 R-precision versus 0.0149 today. Already measured: rrf_k 60->30 costs -0.00579 NDCG@100 (paired 2SE 0.00222, SIGNIFICANT - the shipped harness calls this 'no difference'); tag_exact 0.7->0.9 gains +0.00186 R-prec (paired 2SE 0.00165, significant).

ESTABLISHES: which weights can be discriminated and at what magnitude. DOES NOT: tune anything, make a null result evidence of optimality, or touch mmr_lambda and the sequencer weights, which live past the harness's last stage. Will not rescue audio:0.6 - that channel is inactive on 82.2% of k=0 challenges, a query-set defect no statistic fixes.

ACCEPTANCE: `cadence eval-ab --k 0 --limit 400 --arm rrf_k=30` reproduces delta R-prec -0.00109 +/- 0.00185 and delta NDCG -0.00579 +/- 0.00222, flagging the second detectable and the first not.

Effort: 90 min.

title: Price the audio term against a shuffled-affinity control
description:
The proposed decisive experiment is NOT decisive: held-out membership is co-filing and the folksonomy is co-filing aggregated - asking it to arbitrate is asking a ruler which of two things is longer when one of them is the ruler. It can price the audio term's cost; it can never credit its benefit.

But its CONTROL is decisive. Pilot n=60, paired, precision@20 vs withheld tracks, affinity vector randomly permuted:

  w=0.20  real .1242  shuffled .1117  +0.0125 (t 1.37)
  w=0.35  real .0967  shuffled .1000  -0.0033 (t -0.37)
  w=0.60  real .0442  shuffled .0742  -0.0300 (t -3.18)
  w=0.80  real .0092  shuffled .0408  -0.0317 (t -3.97)

At the shipped 0.35 the audio term is indistinguishable from a random permutation of itself; above 0.45 it is significantly WORSE than noise.

Also measured: only 323 of 2000 held-out titles (16.2%) activate an audio target, so the knob is a literal no-op on 83.8% of the set and any naive full-set eval is diluted ~6x.

ESTABLISHES: the cost of the audio term in held-out-membership units, with a control separating 'points at wrong music' from 'any perturbation of a membership-trained reranker hurts'. DOES NOT: arbitrate which definition of mood-correct is right. Report as pricing, not arbitration.

ACCEPTANCE: artifacts/affinity_membership.json with per-weight real and shuffled means, paired delta and SE, >=5 permutations; states explicitly whether real-shuffled at 0.35 excludes zero at 2xSE; runs under 15 min.

Effort: 150 min.

title: Extend retrieve-once/replay-many to mmr_lambda and give the sweep error bars
description:
run_eval.py never calls engine.generate, so assemble/select.py and sequencer.py never execute and NO number in eval_report.json constrains mmr_lambda (0.72), beam_width (24), or the four sequencer weights - at any n. Pairing does not fix this; it is structural.

affinity_sweep.py already proves the pattern: retrieval is invariant to selection parameters, so it retrieved 294 cases once in 61s then swept 8 weights in 6.6s - 0.83s per extra arm, 74x cheaper than re-retrieving. It applies this to exactly one knob and pins mmr_lambda at the shipped value internally.

It also reports zero standard errors anywhere - every per-case list is collapsed with float(np.mean(v)) - so the affinity sweep's own resolution is unknown.

ESTABLISHES: a priced trade for the one assembly knob that shapes what the listener actually receives. DOES NOT: make mmr_lambda visible to R-precision (the harness still stops at retrieval), cover beam_width or the sequencer weights (which need listening tests), or find an optimum where the trade is smoothly convex.

ACCEPTANCE: eval-affinity writes per-arm SEs and paired deltas; a --knob mmr_lambda --values 0.5,0.6,0.72,0.85,1.0 sweep completes under 3 min reporting tag-strength and intra-list-distance with bands on both.

Effort: 75 min.

title: Wire Segue as an eval-only channel and publish the fused A/B
description:
Prototyped, not argued: collaborative_channel swapped for Segue's operator through Cadence's real fusion and reranker on the frozen splits. Baselines reproduce eval_report.json exactly.

  k=25 reranked R-prec  0.2005 -> 0.2095  paired +0.0090 +/- 0.0027
  k=25 fusion  R-prec   0.1443 -> 0.1508  paired +0.0064 +/- 0.0023

Null at k<=10, inert at k=0 by construction - which is the case EVALUATION.md calls 'the case the project exists for'. The unpaired 2SE is 0.0181, larger than the effect: THE SHIPPED HARNESS WOULD CALL THIS NULL.

Order is what survives: order-attributable share of the clicks win is 0% at k=1, 13% at k=5, 57% at k=10, 101% at k=25. Segue's headline '13.7% average' is majority order-FREE at low k.

Dependency direction: export 0.62MB of beta as an .npz and copy ~35 lines of pure-numpy encoder. Do NOT import segue into cadence - it inverts the star topology and breaks cadence's standalone install.

ESTABLISHES: whether the channel-level win survives fusion. DOES NOT: create a serving surface - seed_indices_from_intent emits resolution order, not listening order, so the channel stays eval-only and returns empty without an ordered prefix. Does not cover k=0.

ACCEPTANCE: eval_report.json carries a sequence cell at every k with paired deltas plus sequence_shuffled and sequence_orderfree arms; EVALUATION.md states the k<=10 null and k=0 inertness as plainly as the k=25 win; cadence's suite passes with segue NOT installed.

Effort: 150-210 min.

title: Verify independently that concentration here is demand-shaped
description:
An agent measured what humans actually put on the same 400 held-out playlists at the same 8,000-slot volume:

  uniform-random draw   gini 0.880  top-1% 21.4%
  Cadence (shown)       gini 0.951  top-1% 43.6%  tail 58.5%
  what humans did       gini 0.965  top-1% 53.7%  tail  6.9%

If it holds, Cadence is LESS concentrated than the demand it is scored against and serves the long tail 8.5x more than the humans did - and the top 1% of artists hold 43.5% of all catalog playlist appearances against Cadence's 43.6% of exposure, i.e. it reproduces the demand distribution almost exactly rather than amplifying it.

That reframes Gamut's headline from 'we failed to fix concentration' to 'concentration is demand-shaped and the measured price of unwinding it is steep'. It is the strongest claim in the whole audit and it is currently single-sourced from one agent run.

ESTABLISHES (if it replicates): that raising catalog reach moves the product away from its target. DOES NOT: settle whether serving demand is the right objective - that is a product and ethical question, not a measurement one, and Gamut's own framing about artist exposure remains live.

ACCEPTANCE: reproduced from a committed script over the same splits, with the random-draw floor included; gamut/README.md and the published page updated only if it replicates; if it does not, say so and keep the original framing.

Effort: 60 min. Blocks any decision about retrieval-side interventions.

title: Share one scoring loop between run_eval and eval-ab
description: score_arm in eval/eval_ab.py duplicates the per-challenge scoring loop in run_eval._run_engine_config almost token for token: the seeds cast, the retrieve(extra_seed_indices=seeds, exclude=seeds, top_n=DEPTH) call, the stable-argsort reranker resort, and acc.update(evaluate_ranking(...)). eval-ab's deltas are only readable against evaluate's levels while the two loops agree on depth, exclusions and reranking, and engine.py's own docstring says duplicating the retrieve path is how offline metrics drift from online behaviour. Raised by the simplicity lens during spot-4ec's self-review and deferred there because the extraction lands in run_eval.py, which PR #9 (spot-7lj) rewrote and which was not in spot-4ec's base - doing it in that PR would have conflicted.
design: Extract score_challenge(engine, ch, intent, artist_ids) -> np.ndarray (or the metrics dict) into run_eval.py. _run_engine_config keeps its timing, exposure and coverage bookkeeping around the call; score_arm collapses to a short for-loop passing the pre-planned intent. The only real difference between the two sites is where the intent comes from, which is one parameter.
acceptance_criteria: Both harnesses call one shared per-challenge scoring helper; cadence evaluate reproduces its current means exactly and the eval-ab tests still pass.
notes: Do this only on a base that already contains PR #9 (spot-7lj) and spot-4ec.
